wind.hs_bearing_damage.name: HS bearing surface damage
wind.hs_bearing_damage.summary: A gearbox high-speed bearing running hotter than its load and the weather explain, rising steadily, with oil debris or vibration moving with it.

pipeline.title: Find peers
pipeline.text: every other HS bearing on the site, counting only points where its turbine has produced for the last 60 min

pipeline.title: Expected value
pipeline.text: fit on the peers: bearing temperature ≈ c0 + c1 × load (40-min average) + c2 × ambient

pipeline.title: Residual
pipeline.text: actual − expected: heat that load and weather don't explain

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: threshold · trend shape · persistence · corroboration · locality

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: all required checks → raise an item; independent supporting checks → confidence

checks.rule: slope(residual, slope_window_min) > min_slope_c_per_h and maxStep(residual since onset) < max_step_c

confidence.high: confirmed by inspection or oil analysis

wind.generator_cooling_loss.name: Generator cooling lost
wind.generator_cooling_loss.summary: Generator windings running far hotter than load and weather explain, because whatever feeds it cooling air (on the cooling relationship layer) has stopped.

pipeline.title: Find peers
pipeline.text: every other generator of the same type, counting only points where its turbine has produced for 60 min

pipeline.title: Expected value
pipeline.text: fit on the peers: winding temperature ≈ c0 + c1 × load (40-min average) + c2 × ambient

pipeline.title: Follow the cooling layer
pipeline.text: the assets that feed this generator on the "cooling" relationship layer — its fan

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: unexplained heat · cooling source stopped · which came first · recovery after restart

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: the symptom is on the generator, the cause is on the asset feeding it

checks.rule: fan < fan_off_a while producing, starting before (or with) the heat
fan stop leads the residual crossing by ≤ lead_max_min
residual < hot_c within recover_within_min of the fan restarting

confidence.high: temperature recovered after the cooling source restarted

wind.feeder_trip.name: Collector feeder trip
wind.feeder_trip.summary: A feeder loses all its turbines in one interval while the wind is fine; the detector then looks down the feeder for the one asset that was already misbehaving beforehand.

pipeline.title: Trip
pipeline.text: feeder output falls to near zero within one interval

pipeline.title: Common cause
pipeline.text: every turbine on the feeder dropped in the same interval, and the wind was fine

pipeline.title: Look for the origin
pipeline.text: each pad transformer on the feeder against a fleet model of oil temperature for its load and ambient, over the hour before the trip

pipeline.title: Contain
pipeline.text: other feeders unaffected; after restoration, which turbine stayed off

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: upstream common point, origin named when one asset trended abnormally first

checks.rule: feeder > min_before_kw, then < drop_to_frac × that in one interval
all child turbines ≈ 0 in the same interval
one pad transformer residual rose > origin_rise_c in origin_window_min before the trip
feeder restored with the origin turbine left off

confidence.high: origin found and the feeder held once it was isolated

wind.anemometer_fault.name: Nacelle anemometer reading wrong
wind.anemometer_fault.summary: A turbine's own wind reading disagrees with its neighbours, while everything the wind actually drives — power, rotor speed — agrees with them. The instrument is wrong, not the process.

pipeline.title: Neighbours
pipeline.text: the other turbines on the same feeder that are producing

pipeline.title: Compare
pipeline.text: this turbine's wind reading and its power, each as a share of the neighbours' median

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: reading disagrees · power agrees · rotor speed agrees · icing weather

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: nothing physical confirms the odd reading, so it's the sensor

checks.rule: ambient < icing_temp_c and humidity ≥ icing_rh_pct at onset and for ≥ 75 % of the episode

confidence.high: reading recovered after a sensor action

wind.converter_condensation_trip.name: Converter trip from condensation
wind.converter_condensation_trip.summary: A turbine drops out on its own (its feeder stays up) with the converter cabinet unusually humid and the converter itself not hot: moisture, not heat, caused the trip.

pipeline.title: Trip
pipeline.text: the turbine goes from producing to zero in one interval while its feeder neighbours keep running

pipeline.title: Before the trip
pipeline.text: cabinet humidity in the hour before, against every other converter on site

pipeline.title: Rule out heat
pipeline.text: converter temperature at the trip against the fleet

pipeline.title: Context
pipeline.text: hours of cold, low-load running beforehand — when condensation forms

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: humid and not hot → condensation; confirmation needs an inspection

inputs.neighbours: unit siblings on the same feeder

checks.rule: unit power > min_before_kw, then ≈ 0, neighbours still producing
ambient < 0 °C and load < low_load_frac for most of context_window_h
humidity above every other converter for the hours before

wind.pitch_battery_weak.name: Pitch backup battery failing
wind.pitch_battery_weak.summary: Short safety stops, each with the blades moving toward feather, repeating on one turbine while its pitch backup battery voltage sits below the fleet and keeps falling.

pipeline.title: Find the stops
pipeline.text: intervals where output falls by half against the intervals either side, with the blades pitched toward feather and the wind steady

pipeline.title: Count them
pipeline.text: how many in the last 3 hours, and whether they are getting closer together

pipeline.title: Battery
pipeline.text: backup battery voltage against every other pitch system on site

pipeline.title: Rule out
pipeline.text: grid events (other turbines didn't stop), gusts, pitch motor faults

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: repeated battery-test stops → the pack can't guarantee a feather on grid loss

checks.rule: ≥ min_stops stops in window_min (output < drop_frac × neighbours in time, pitch > feather_deg)
no other turbine stopped in the same intervals

confidence.high: every stop lines up with a feathering and the battery is below the test limit

wind.static_yaw_misalignment.name: Static yaw misalignment
wind.static_yaw_misalignment.summary: A turbine that never stops but steadily makes a few percent less than its neighbours, pointed a fixed angle off the wind that its own vane can't see.

pipeline.title: Neighbours
pipeline.text: the other turbines on the same feeder that are producing

pipeline.title: Performance gap
pipeline.text: 6-hour average power-curve performance against the neighbours' median

pipeline.title: Pointing
pipeline.text: nacelle direction against the met-mast wind direction, averaged over the same 6 hours

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: gap · always available · fixed offset · vane says 0° · cos-law size

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: a steady offset the controller can't see explains the loss

wind.blade_icing.name: Blade icing
wind.blade_icing.summary: Several turbines in one string lose power-curve performance together in freezing, saturated air, and recover as it warms: weather, not a machine fault.

pipeline.title: Performance
pipeline.text: 30-minute average power-curve performance on each producing turbine

pipeline.title: Weather
pipeline.text: met-mast ambient temperature and humidity: icing needs both cold and moisture

pipeline.title: Shared
pipeline.text: how many turbines on the same feeder are losing performance at the same time

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: loss · icing weather · shared · no faults · recovery with warming

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: shared, weather-timed loss → icing; one item per feeder, on the worst turbine

checks.rule: ambient < icing_temp_c and humidity > icing_rh_pct at detection
≥ min_shared turbines on the feeder below low_pct together

wind.curtailment_compliance.name: Curtailment instruction at risk
wind.curtailment_compliance.summary: An export cap is coming, export is above it and rising with the wind, and the setpoint that would hold it isn't in yet.

pipeline.title: Instruction
pipeline.text: the grid operator's export cap and when it starts (from the dispatch feed)

pipeline.title: Now
pipeline.text: export against the cap, and its trend over the last hour

pipeline.title: Plan
pipeline.text: is the setpoint task done, and how long is left before the cap starts

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: an action with a deadline, not a diagnosis

inputs.setpoint task: work item for this asset from the instruction

checks.rule: export > capKw while the cap is pending

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: HS bearing temperature against what we'd expect for this turbine's load and today's weather. The shaded gap is heat that load and weather don't explain.

checks.label: Hotter than expected for its load
checks.value: +12.7 °C above expected now. Alert level is +5 °C.
checks.why: Bearing damage adds friction heat that load and weather can't explain.

checks.label: Rising steadily, not jumping
checks.value: +1.2 °C per hour over the last 2 h. Largest 10-min step: 0.8 °C.
checks.why: Wear grows gradually. A sensor or wiring fault usually shows up as a sudden jump.

checks.label: Sustained, not a passing spike
checks.value: Above +5 °C since 09:00 (5 h). Above +2 °C since 07:30.
checks.why: Needs at least 1 h above the alert level, so gusts and restarts don't trigger it.

checks.label: Oil debris rising
checks.value: About 4 particles/h before 07:30, 22 now. Other turbines: 2–5.
checks.why: A separate sensor. Metal flaking off a damaged bearing race ends up in the oil.

checks.label: Bearing vibration up
checks.value: 3.42 mm/s. Other turbines: 2.31–2.57 mm/s.
checks.why: A damaged rolling surface makes the bearing run rougher.

checks.label: Heat stays local to this bearing
checks.value: Main bearing 36.2 °C (fleet 33.9–37.6). Generator bearing normal.
checks.why: A cooling or lubrication problem would warm the whole drivetrain, not one bearing.

references.title: Confirmed spalling
references.description: Fully developed case. Heat and debris climb together until the bearing is replaced.
notes: Same gradual climb, at a similar rate
Debris rising alongside, as here

references.title: Caught early
references.description: What it looks like while there is still plenty of time. Easy to miss, since it stays under most alarm limits.
notes: WTG-05 has passed this stage
Shows what to watch for on other turbines

references.title: Sensor offset, not damage
references.description: A loose connection makes the reading jump. The bearing itself is healthy.
notes: This jumps in one step; WTG-05 climbs
Debris stays flat here; on WTG-05 it rose 6×

ruledOut.reason: WTG-05 is producing 2,298 kW. The other running Feeder 1 turbines are at 2,238–2,300 kW, and read 75–76 °C.
Ambient went from −5.6 to 2.5 °C today, but the expected-temperature model allows for it, and every other running turbine stayed within ±2.9 °C of expected all day:

chart.caption: Unexplained heat: WTG-05 against 16 other turbines.

ruledOut.reason: The rise is gradual (largest 10-min step 0.8 °C), and two separate sensors, oil debris and vibration, moved with it.
Main and generator bearings read normal for the fleet. Gearbox oil is only 3.3 °C above the fleet median, which fits heat coming from one bearing rather than a cooler failure.

BSIT01.excluded: Left out of the comparison: WTG-02 (planned maintenance) and WTG-10 (down). Turbines that are stopped don't tell us what "normal at this load" looks like.

confidence.because: Heat and oil debris are measured by independent sensors and both point at this bearing.
confidence.notHigherBecause: Nobody has inspected it yet. SCADA can't tell spalling from lubrication starvation at one bearing.
confidence.raiseIf: The oil sample shows ferrous wear particles, or the borescope shows spalling on the HS race.
confidence.lowerIf: The oil sample is clean. Then recheck the sensor and the bearing's lube supply.

action.text: Keep running with a lower temperature alarm; schedule borescope and oil sample at the next low-wind window; order a replacement bearing kit.

conclusion.label: Cause
conclusion.text: Cooling fan stopped; the generator itself was healthy
conclusion.confidenceText: Confirmed: temperature fell as soon as the fan restarted

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: Stator winding temperature against what this load and today's weather would explain. The shaded gap is heat the cooling system didn't remove.

checks.label: Windings far hotter than load explains
checks.value: Peaked at 137.4 °C at 11:10, +45 °C above expected for its load.
checks.why: Load and weather set how much heat the generator makes. Heat beyond that points at cooling.

checks.label: Its cooling fan had stopped
checks.value: Fan motor current fell from about 7.1 A to 0.0 A at 09:40, with the turbine still producing.
checks.why: The fan feeds this generator on the cooling layer. Without it, heat stays in the windings.

checks.label: The fan stopped first
checks.value: The fan stopped at 09:40; the windings left normal 10 min later, at 09:50.
checks.why: A cause comes before its effect. If the windings had heated first, the fan would be a victim, not the cause.

checks.label: Temperature fell once the fan restarted
checks.value: Fan back at 11:20; windings back within +15 °C of expected by 11:50.
checks.why: Restoring the cause and watching the symptom clear is the strongest confirmation there is.

references.title: Fan trip, reset in time
references.description: The fan motor protection trips; the windings climb until the fan is reset, then fall straight back.
notes: Fan current to zero, then the heat
Recovery as soon as the fan restarts

references.title: Clogged air filter
references.description: The fan still runs but moves less air. The windings run a little warm for days before anyone notices.
notes: Fan current drops but not to zero
Worth checking filters at the next visit

references.title: Winding hot spot, fan healthy
references.description: An internal winding fault makes heat the fan can't remove. The fan current stays normal throughout.
notes: Here the fan runs normally; on WTG-03 it stopped
A hot spot wouldn't clear when a fan restarts

ruledOut.reason: The heat input didn't change, the heat removal did: the windings came back to normal by 11:50 once the fan restarted, with no repair to the generator.
Output was 1,132 kW when the heating began and 1,624 kW at the peak. The expected-temperature line already allows for that, and the actual temperature ran +45 °C above it.
Ambient was −0.7 °C when the heating began and 0.7 °C at the peak.
A second, independent signal — the fan current — explains the rise, and the reading fell exactly when the fan came back.

confidence.because: The fan stopped first, the windings heated, and they cooled again when it restarted.
confidence.lowerIf: The windings stay hot with the fan running. Then suspect the generator itself.

action.text: Reset the fan motor breaker, then watch the winding temperature come back down before closing out.

model.fittedOn: 18 generators of the same type, running points today

conclusion.label: Cause
conclusion.text: Internal fault in WTG-10's pad transformer, cleared by the Feeder 2 breaker
conclusion.confidenceText: Confirmed: Feeder 2 held once WTG-10 was isolated

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: Feeder 2 output through the day. Everything on the feeder stopped at once, with the wind still blowing.

checks.label: Feeder output fell to zero in one interval
checks.why: Losing a whole feeder at once is a breaker opening, not turbines winding down.

checks.label: All 7 turbines dropped together
checks.value: 7 of 7 Feeder 2 turbines lost power in the same 10-minute interval.
checks.why: When every turbine stops at the same moment, the cause is the point they share — the feeder — not each machine.

checks.label: The wind was fine
checks.value: 8.6 m/s at the met mast at 10:10 — well inside the operating range.
checks.why: Rules out a calm or a storm shutdown.

checks.label: One asset was misbehaving first: WTG-10 pad transformer
checks.value: Its oil ran +16.2 °C hotter than its load explains in the hour before the trip, at 53 % load. The other transformers on Feeder 2 stayed within +1.8 °C.
checks.why: A transformer heating with no extra load has an internal fault. If its own protection doesn't clear it, the feeder breaker does — taking every turbine with it.

checks.label: Other feeders unaffected
checks.value: Feeder 1, Feeder 3 and Feeder 4 kept producing through 10:10.
checks.why: A substation or grid event would have hit every feeder.

checks.label: Feeder held once WTG-10 was left off
checks.value: Re-energised at 10:50 with 6 of 7 turbines; WTG-10 stayed off.
checks.why: If the feeder holds without the suspect, the suspect was the fault.

references.title: Pad transformer fault
references.description: One transformer heats for up to an hour, then faults. The feeder breaker clears it and the feeder comes back without that turbine.
notes: A warning an hour ahead on one transformer
Back without the faulty turbine

references.title: Cable or splice fault
references.description: Same trip, no warning: underground cable faults rarely show anything beforehand. The whole feeder stays off until the fault is found.
notes: Feeder 2 had a clear warning; a cable fault wouldn't
Different follow-up: cable test, not transformer test

references.title: Storm shutdown
references.description: Wind above cut-out speed: turbines stop one by one over half an hour. Nothing is broken.
notes: Turbines stop one at a time, not together
Today the wind was only 8.6 m/s

ruledOut.reason: 8.6 m/s at the met mast when the feeder tripped.
Feeder 1, Feeder 3 and Feeder 4 kept producing; export fell only by Feeder 2's share.
All 7 stopped in the same interval — they share one breaker.
Only WTG-10's transformer ran hot beforehand:

chart.caption: Pad transformer oil above what its load explains, every turbine on Feeder 2.

confidence.because: The whole feeder stopped at once with good wind, WTG-10's transformer was the only asset trending abnormally beforehand, and the feeder held without it.
confidence.lowerIf: A transformer test on WTG-10 comes back clean. Then test the feeder cable.

action.text: Isolate WTG-10 at its loop-feed switches, re-energise Feeder 2, and keep WTG-10 out of service for transformer testing.

conclusion.label: Cause
conclusion.text: Iced nacelle anemometer — the instrument was wrong, the turbine was fine
conclusion.confidenceText: Confirmed: the reading recovered once the heater was reset

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: WTG-12's own wind reading against the other Feeder 2 turbines. The shaded band is their range.

checks.label: Its wind reading disagrees with its neighbours
checks.value: 3.5 m/s at 07:30, against 6.8 m/s on the other Feeder 2 turbines (−49 %). Low from 06:40 to 09:40.
checks.why: One reading out of line with every neighbour is either a local weather effect or a bad sensor.

checks.label: Its power agrees with its neighbours
checks.value: 536 kW at 07:30, −7 % against the neighbours' median.
checks.why: If the wind really were that low, the turbine couldn't make this much power.

checks.label: Rotor speed agrees too
checks.value: Within 5 % of the neighbours throughout.
checks.why: A second physical measurement of the same wind, from a different sensor.

checks.label: Its performance figure looks impossible
checks.value: Power-curve performance, computed from its own wind reading, sat at 130 % or more.
checks.why: A turbine can't beat its power curve by 30 %. The input to that calculation is wrong.

checks.label: Icing weather at the time
checks.value: Ambient −5.0 to −0.9 °C, humidity 90–96 % while it read low.
checks.why: Freezing fog ices unheated cups and vanes — the usual reason a nacelle anemometer reads low.

checks.label: Reading recovered after the heater reset
checks.value: Back within 10 % of the neighbours at 09:50.
checks.why: Fixing the sensor fixed the reading, and nothing else changed.

references.title: Iced anemometer
references.description: The cups ice up in freezing fog and read 30–50 % low. Power and rotor speed carry on as normal.
notes: Wind reading drops, power doesn't
Freezing fog at the time

references.title: Worn anemometer bearing
references.description: The reading drifts low over days as the bearing drags. Same "power disagrees" signature, slower.
notes: Drop here is gradual, not a step
Replace the sensor rather than reset the heater

references.title: Real local lull (wake)
references.description: A neighbour's wake really slows the wind at this turbine. Power falls with the reading.
notes: Power fell here; on WTG-12 it didn't
A wake depends on wind direction, not on icing weather

ruledOut.cause: Genuinely low wind at this turbine
ruledOut.reason: Power and rotor speed matched the neighbours, and the met mast read 6.7 m/s at 07:30.
Output was normal for the wind the neighbours saw. The high performance figure comes from the bad reading.
A wake lowers power as well as the wind reading. Here power didn't drop.

confidence.because: Two independent physical measurements, power and rotor speed, say the wind was normal.
confidence.lowerIf: Power falls to match the reading. Then the wind really is lower at this turbine.
confidence.confirmedBy: Reading recovered after the heater reset

action.text: Reset the anemometer heater and confirm the reading returns to the met-mast reference.

conclusion.label: Most likely cause
conclusion.text: Condensation in the converter cabinet tripped the phase module
conclusion.confidenceText: Humid and cool at the trip; not inspected yet

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: Converter cabinet humidity against every other converter on site (shaded).

checks.label: Tripped on its own
checks.value: 1,952 kW at 12:20, 0 kW at 12:30. The rest of its feeder kept producing.
checks.why: A trip on one turbine, with its neighbours unaffected, starts inside that turbine.

checks.label: Cabinet humid before the trip
checks.value: Humidity reached 72 % in the hour before. Other converters: 32–39 %.
checks.why: Above about 65 %, moisture can condense on cold power electronics and track across them.

checks.label: The converter wasn't hot
checks.value: 48.5 °C just before the trip. Other converters: 48.4–51.6 °C.
checks.why: Rules out the usual thermal causes: overload, cooling failure, a failing module running hot.

checks.label: A cold, low-load morning first
checks.value: 3 h 10 min of the 6 h before the trip were below 0 °C at under 40 % load.
checks.why: At low load the converter makes little heat, so a cold cabinet cools below the dew point. The trip then comes as load ramps up.

checks.label: More humid than every other converter
checks.value: Above the rest of the fleet continuously from 00:00 to the trip.
checks.why: The weather was the same for every turbine. Something local — a heater or a seal — let this one get damp.

checks.label: Restarted, humidity falling
checks.value: Back at 13:10 after the cabinet heaters ran; humidity 65 % then, 52 % now.
checks.why: Drying the cabinet let it run again. That fits condensation, though it doesn't prove it.

checks.label: Moisture found on the phase module
checks.value: Not inspected yet.
checks.why: Only a look inside the cabinet (tracking marks, corrosion) confirms condensation.

references.title: Condensation trip
references.description: Humidity creeps up through a cold, quiet night. The converter trips as load ramps up, running cool.
notes: Humid and cool at the trip
Came back once the heaters dried it out

references.title: Heaters caught it
references.description: Same humid night, but the cabinet heater brought humidity down before load came back. No trip.
notes: What a correctly set heater looks like
Check the heater thermostat on WTG-09

references.title: Thermal trip
references.description: A blocked cooling path or failing module runs hot and trips on temperature. Humidity is normal.
notes: Hot converter here; WTG-09's was cool
Humidity normal here

ruledOut.reason: Converter temperature was 48.5 °C, inside the fleet range.
The other turbines on the feeder kept producing through the trip.
The turbine restarted and is running, which a dead module wouldn't allow. Moisture damage can still weaken it, so it needs a look at the next visit.

confidence.because: The cabinet was humid, the converter was cool, and it tripped on a load ramp after a cold, low-load morning — the pattern field studies link to condensation.
confidence.notHigherBecause: Nobody has looked inside the cabinet yet.
confidence.raiseIf: The inspection finds moisture tracking or corrosion on the phase module.
confidence.lowerIf: The module is clean and dry. Then look at the module's own health and the trip log.

action.text: Keep running; check the cabinet heater thermostat and inspect the phase module for moisture tracking at the next visit.

conclusion.label: Most likely cause
conclusion.text: Pitch backup battery pack at end of life
conclusion.confidenceText: Low voltage and repeated battery-test stops agree

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: Pitch backup battery voltage against every other pitch system on site (shaded). Markers are the safety stops.

checks.label: 4 safety stops since 11:50
checks.value: At 11:50, 12:40, 13:20 and 13:50. Each cut that interval's output by about 64 %, with the blades pitched to 58° and the wind steady.
checks.why: A pitch system tests its backup battery and feathers the blades when the test fails. Each one is small; together they are a pattern.

checks.label: Backup battery below the fleet and the test limit
checks.value: 205.6 V now (nominal about 238 V). Every other pitch system: 236.6–240.0 V.
checks.why: The backup battery is what feathers the blades if the grid is lost. Below the limit, it may not be able to.

checks.label: Voltage still falling
checks.value: −2.4 V per hour over the last 6 h; 230.4 V at 00:00.
checks.why: A pack that is losing capacity sags further as the cold soaks in. It won't recover on its own.

checks.label: Stops coming closer together
checks.value: 50 min, 40 min and 30 min apart.
checks.why: Each test is failing sooner. The next step is a stop that doesn't restart, or a feather that doesn't happen.

checks.label: No other turbine stopped at those times
checks.value: The other 23 turbines kept producing through all 4 stops.
checks.why: A grid disturbance would stop many turbines at once. This is one machine.

references.title: End-of-life pack in the cold
references.description: Voltage sags below the test limit; battery tests fail and stop the turbine, closer and closer together.
notes: Voltage under the limit and falling
Stops getting more frequent

charts.title: Battery voltage (hours from the first stop)
Output (% of the intervals either side)

references.title: Ageing pack, no stops yet
references.description: Voltage below the fleet and drifting down, but still above the limit. Nothing trips yet.
notes: The time to plan a pack swap
Worth checking other packs of the same age

charts.title: Battery voltage (hours from the first stop)
Output (% of the intervals either side)

references.title: Grid voltage dips
references.description: Short stops caused by the grid. Many turbines stop at once, and batteries are normal.
notes: Batteries healthy here
Only WTG-14 stopped today

charts.title: Battery voltage (hours from the first stop)
Output (% of the intervals either side)

ruledOut.reason: No other turbine stopped in the same intervals.
Wind at the met mast was 11.2–12.5 m/s at the stops, far below cut-out.
Between stops the pitch motor drew 4.7 A on average; the other pitch systems drew 4.6–5.8 A over the same time. The drive works; the battery is the problem.

confidence.because: The battery is below the test limit and every stop is a feathering on this turbine alone.
confidence.lowerIf: A new pack still fails the test. Then check the charger and wiring.

action.text: Stop WTG-14 and keep it stopped until the battery pack is replaced — without it, the blades may not feather on a grid loss.

BSIT06.impact: About 922 kWh lost to stops so far today; the bigger risk is safety, not energy.

conclusion.label: Most likely cause
conclusion.text: Wind vane offset — the turbine points about 11° off the wind
conclusion.confidenceText: Offset and output loss agree in size

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: Power-curve performance, 1-hour average, against the other Feeder 3 turbines (shaded: their 10-minute range).

checks.label: Steadily below its Feeder 3 neighbours
checks.value: 94.8 % of its power curve today, against 99.5 % for the other Feeder 3 turbines (−4.7 points). The last 6 h: −4.8 points.
checks.why: Neighbours see nearly the same wind, so a steady gap is the turbine, not the weather.

checks.label: Never stopped
checks.value: Available 100 % of the time today, with no fault codes.
checks.why: This is why the loss hides: availability and alarms say everything is fine.

checks.label: Pointed about 11° off the wind
checks.value: Nacelle direction averaged −10.8° from the met-mast wind direction all day (± 1.8°). Its neighbours average within ±1°.
checks.why: A rotor that isn't facing the wind catches less of it. A fixed offset like this is set up, not random.

checks.label: Its own vane says it's aligned
checks.value: Measured yaw error averaged −0.4°.
checks.why: The controller steers by the vane. If the vane itself is offset, the controller can't see the error.

checks.label: The loss is the size the offset predicts
checks.value: A 11° offset should cost about 4.4 % (cos-law); the measured gap is 4.7 points.
checks.why: Two independent measurements — pointing and output — tell the same story in the same amount.

references.title: Vane offset after maintenance
references.description: A replaced or knocked vane leaves a fixed pointing error. Output sits 4–6 % low from that day on.
notes: Same steady gap
Same fixed offset, invisible to the vane

references.title: Small offset
references.description: A 4° offset costs about 1 % — lost in the noise of any single day, visible over a few weeks.
notes: Why this is often found months later
Worth screening every turbine

references.title: Blade soiling or erosion
references.description: Dirty or eroded leading edges cost a similar few percent, but the turbine points straight into the wind.
notes: No offset here; WTG-17 is 11° off
Fix is a blade inspection, not a vane

ruledOut.reason: It was below freezing overnight, but the gap stayed the same after ambient rose to 2.5 °C, and its Feeder 3 neighbours weren't affected.
No setpoint was active, and blade pitch followed the wind as normal (about 0.5° on average).
It would cost output without any pointing error. The offset alone explains the size of the loss.

confidence.because: The nacelle points off the wind by a fixed angle, and the output loss is the size that angle predicts.
confidence.notHigherBecause: Nobody has checked the vane on site yet, and the met mast is one reference for the whole site.
confidence.raiseIf: The vane's north mark is found out of line with the nacelle axis.
confidence.lowerIf: The vane is aligned. Then check the met-mast direction reference and the blades.

action.text: Check the vane’s north-mark alignment against the nacelle axis and correct the offset parameter.

BSIT07.impact: About 1.0 MWh lost today — about 4.7 % of this turbine's output until the vane is corrected.

conclusion.label: Cause
conclusion.text: Rime ice on the blades of the Feeder 4 string
conclusion.confidenceText: Confirmed: output recovered with the thaw

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: Power-curve performance for every Feeder 4 turbine. The loss starts together, deepens through the coldest hours and clears with the thaw.

checks.label: Output well under its power curve
checks.value: 77.5 % of its power curve at 08:20 (30-min average), under 90 % from 05:40 to 10:10.
checks.why: Ice on the blades spoils their shape, so the same wind makes less power.

checks.label: Icing weather
checks.value: −4.4 °C and 96 % humidity at the met mast when it was flagged.
checks.why: Rime ice needs both: air below freezing and moisture to freeze.

checks.label: 3 of 5 Feeder 4 turbines affected together
checks.why: A machine fault hits one turbine. A whole string losing output together is something they share — the weather.

checks.label: No stops, no fault codes
checks.value: WTG-22 kept running through the whole episode.
checks.why: Icing costs output gradually. It doesn't trip the machine unless the controller detects heavy imbalance.

checks.label: Other feeders unaffected
checks.value: The other feeders' turbines were at 100 % (median) at the same time.
checks.why: Feeder 4 is the exposed ridge-top string; the lower strings stayed clear.

checks.label: Recovered as it warmed
checks.value: Ambient crossed 0 °C at 10:20; WTG-22 was back above 95 % by 10:20.
checks.why: Ice sheds as the air warms. Recovery timed with the thaw is the confirmation.

references.title: Rime icing, cleared by the thaw
references.description: Freezing fog builds ice over a few hours; output falls 15–25 %, then recovers as the air goes above 0 °C.
notes: Same depth and timing
Recovery lined up with the thaw

references.title: Light icing
references.description: A thin layer costs 5 % or so — easy to mistake for a poor wind day.
notes: The other Feeder 4 turbines looked like this
Worth an ice-throw check even at this level

references.title: One turbine's own fault
references.description: A pitch or yaw problem costs output on one machine, in any weather, and doesn't clear by itself.
notes: Warm weather here
Here only one turbine; on Feeder 4 it was the whole string

ruledOut.reason: 3 of 5 turbines on Feeder 4 lost output together, with no stops or fault codes.
No export limit was active until this afternoon's instruction.
An iced anemometer reads low and makes performance look high, not low.

confidence.because: The loss was shared across the string, happened only in freezing fog, and cleared as it warmed.
confidence.lowerIf: One turbine stays low after the thaw. Then look at that machine on its own.

action.text: Keep running while ice-throw risk is managed (access restrictions); watch recovery as it warms.

conclusion.label: What's needed
conclusion.text: Enter a 45 MW export setpoint before 14:30

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: Export at the point of interconnection against the 45 MW cap that starts at 14:30.

checks.label: Export is above the coming cap
checks.value: 53.4 MW now; the cap is 45.0 MW from 14:30 (8.4 MW over).
checks.why: Without a setpoint, the plant will keep exporting whatever the wind gives.

checks.label: The setpoint isn't in yet
checks.value: Task "Enter 45 MW curtailment setpoint" is open, due 14:20.
checks.why: The plant controller spreads a site setpoint across turbines automatically, once it's entered.

checks.label: Export rising with the wind
checks.value: +4.6 MW per hour over the last hour; met-mast wind 12.7 m/s. At this rate, about 55.7 MW by 14:30.
checks.why: The gap to close is growing, not shrinking on its own.

checks.label: 30 min until the cap starts
checks.value: Instruction received 13:45 from grid operator. The setpoint task is due at 14:20, leaving time to ramp down.
checks.why: Turbines ramp down over minutes, so the setpoint has to go in before the cap starts, not at it.

references.title: Setpoint in on time
references.description: Setpoint entered 20 minutes ahead; the plant ramps down and is under the cap before it starts.
notes: This is the target
Confirm with the grid operator once it holds

references.title: Setpoint entered late
references.description: Entered at the start time: export stays over the cap for 15–20 minutes while turbines ramp down.
notes: Non-compliance penalties apply to the overshoot
Ramp-down takes minutes, not seconds

references.title: Wind drops on its own
references.description: The wind falls and export goes under the cap without any action. Only safe if the forecast says so.
notes: Wind is rising: 12.7 m/s now
Relying on it risks a penalty

confidence.because: This is an instruction from the grid operator, not something the data had to diagnose.

action.text: Enter the 45 MW setpoint in the power plant controller by 14:20 and confirm it with the grid operator.
